HIL-SERL Implementation — what WE built today (and what we'll do tomorrow)

Sister doc to hilserl_walkthrough.html. That one explains the TEXTBOOK HIL-SERL (Luo et al. paper). This one explains what we simplified, what we shipped, where we are right now, and the 3-day plan to evaluate the policy.

YOU ARE HERE: scaffolding ✓ pre-flight 1-3 ✓ 5090 dataset conversion (running ~20 min) USB enum (Test 4) at-robot Day 1

1. The task we're actually solving (TA-spec, no embellishment)

The TA gives us five rollouts at evaluation. Each rollout is 10 points if the policy picks the correct-color block and places it in the bowl. Crucially, which color and where the bowl sits are randomized per rollout — neither is known at policy-design time. We don't get to pick the yellow scene every time at TA eval. v1 ignores that; v1.5 addresses it.

2. The simplification ladder — what we cut to ship v1 tomorrow

The four decisions came out of yesterday's plan-eng-review:

  • D8 (SmolVLA's role): Option A — SmolVLA stays a parallel BC baseline (already trained, deployable today). HIL-SERL trains its own SAC policy from fresh demos. Why not Option C? lerobot's SAC hardcodes a ResNet-10 actor; transplanting SmolVLA's encoder is a multi-day fork.
  • D1 (color scope): Option C — ONE policy for yellow only. ~15 demos vs ~90 for 6 colors. The 5090 dataset conversion (running NOW) unlocks the multi-color v1.5 path without more teleop.
  • D2 (bowl pose): Train at the fixed (-15.5, 29.5) cm pose. Goal-conditioning would require a custom GoalConditioningProcessorStep because lerobot 0.5.2's ObservationConfig has no documented hook for arbitrary goal vectors.
  • D3 (reward): Manual keyboard reward (s / esc) for v1. HF doc explicitly endorses this for round 1. Trained classifier is v1.5.
The CEO-review question: are we cutting too much? Each simplification has a quantifiable upgrade path. If v1 succeeds at all, the multi-color dataset is already converting on the 5090 → v1.5 is 1 training run away, not 1 teleop session. If bowl-OOD fails, we have the data + URDF to add the goal-conditioning step in v1.5b. The simplifications are cheap to reverse, hard to revisit during the semester clock.

3. Where things run — two machines + HF Hub

The actor↔learner split is HIL-SERL's signature. Without it, the 10 Hz control loop on the Mac would compete with the SAC update for CPU/GPU time and the arm would stall mid-episode. With gRPC, the Mac only does inference (MPS is enough for a ResNet-10 + MLP at 10 Hz) and the 5090 burns its CUDA on the REDQ-10 ensemble + UTD=10-20 SAC updates.

4. The training data flow — three phases

Two things to internalize about this flow:

  1. The demo buffer is the imitation prior — it never empties, and every minibatch is 128 demos + 128 online (the RLPD 50/50 split). It's what keeps the policy from drifting after thousands of online steps.
  2. Your interventions are double-counted — when you grab the leader mid-rollout to rescue a doomed grasp, that transition lands in the intervention buffer AND gets aliased into the demo buffer. The critic learns from it as RL data; the actor learns from it as imitation data.

5. Where we are RIGHT NOW — full state machine

The "you are here" marker sits right after S6 (git push) and just before S8 (the USB enumeration test). S7 — the multi-color dataset conversion on the 5090 — is running in parallel and doesn't block any S8+ step.

6. The two parallel tracks — same wall-clock, different machines

7. Day-3 decision tree — what we do based on eval results

The single most important Day-3 question isn't "did HIL-SERL beat SmolVLA?" — it's "does the policy fail catastrophically when the bowl moves 3 cm?". If it does, that failure mode is invisible at the trained bowl pose but guaranteed to bite at TA eval time (where bowl is randomized). That's why the bowl-OOD probe is non-negotiable.

Open questions (deferred to the lab)

  • D4 — Learner location. 5090 over SSH/gRPC vs. Mac MPS. Resolution: run ping / iperf3 probe from the lab; if median RTT < 5 ms, keep learner on 5090.
  • USB enumeration on Mac. The ports /dev/tty.usbmodem5B141128171 (leader) and /dev/tty.usbmodem5B141129871 (follower) baked into our configs may swap after a reboot. Test 4 of pre-flight confirms.
  • SmolVLA end-to-end after transformers upgrade. Import works; bash deploy/infer_smolvla.sh with the arm is the real test, untested yet.
  • Top camera. Playbook claims +10-20 pp on SmolVLA from a top cam. Open question for the teammate at the robot.

9. The minimum-viable path from now to a deployed policy

Once the user types ls /dev/tty.usbmodem* and confirms two ports show up, the rest is a sequence of well-defined commands from notes/hilserl_lab_checklist.md:

# At the robot
PY=/Users/admin/miniforge3/bin/python3.13

# 1. find EE bounds (drive leader through workspace)
$PY -m lerobot.find_joint_limits   --robot.type=so101_follower   --robot.port=/dev/tty.usbmodem5B141129871   --teleop.type=so101_leader   --teleop.port=/dev/tty.usbmodem5B141128171
# → paste printed bounds into sim/hilserl/configs/env_config_so101.json

# 2. record 15 yellow demos
bash teleop/record_hilserl_demos.sh

# 3. pick the wrist-image ROI
$PY -m lerobot.rl.crop_dataset_roi --repo-id osammotg1/projet3-hilserl-yellow-v1
# → paste printed crop into both env_config + train_config

# 4. on the 5090 (SSH): start the learner
$PY -m lerobot.rl.learner --config_path sim/hilserl/configs/train_config_hilserl_so101.json

# 5. on the Mac (separate terminal): start the actor + intervene
$PY -m lerobot.rl.actor --config_path sim/hilserl/configs/train_config_hilserl_so101.json

# 6. eval (Day 3)
#    5 primary rollouts + 5 bowl-OOD rollouts → submit best policy
The whole HIL-SERL apparatus comes down to those 6 commands once the configs are in place. Everything we built today existed so that these commands would actually work when you run them — the URDF, the IK config, the env JSON, the train JSON, the shared teleop plumbing, the conversion script, the handoff doc.
